[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Find K Closest Elements** [LC 658 · Find K Closest Elements](https://leetcode.com/problems/find-k-closest-elements/){difficulty="Medium"}

The array is sorted, so the $k$ closest elements are not scattered: they form a **consecutive window** $\mathit{arr}[l..l+k-1]$. (Exchange argument: if the chosen set skips an element that lies between two chosen ones, that skipped element is at least as close as the farther of the two outer chosen elements, so swapping it in never hurts.) That turns "choose $k$ of $n$" into "choose **one** number, the window's start $l$", a search over the $n - k + 1$ starts. Comparing window $l$ with window $l + 1$ only involves the element that leaves, $\mathit{arr}[l]$, and the element that enters, $\mathit{arr}[l+k]$, and the answer "move right?" flips from yes to no exactly once as $l$ grows. Binary search that flip.

[Solved in full in @sec-bst-p2-a.]{.card-link}
